notes: %WoE_Cal (PROC FREQ + PROC TRANSPOSE + PROC SQL Weight-of-Evidence calculation) is byte-identical to the source macro definition. The source driver read Dev/Val from an external libname ('F:\AMIT\TVS', not available here), so this bundle supplies small mock Dev/Val datasets with the same column shape the macro expects (a pre-binned LTV_B variable + the gbi_tag 0/1 dependent variable). The PROC FREQ crosstab and PROC TRANSPOSE run correctly and reproduce real counts. The final Woe column (log of a remerged Good/Bad ratio via PROC SQL - 'log((Good/sum(Good))/(Bad/sum(bad))) as Woe', a standard SAS PROC SQL remerge pattern) comes back as missing for every row - Jenner 0.1.0 silently returns status ok with missing values for log() applied to a remerged-aggregate ratio expression once a non-aggregate column is also selected (a related, simpler case without the extra column throws a hard DataFusion GROUP BY planning error instead). Both are genuine, reproducible Jenner defects in PROC SQL aggregate remerging, filed upstream as regression tests in set/ - not a bundle authoring error, so the missing Woe values are captured as-is.
